name: Rice
how_to_identify_leaf: Long, flat, slender linear blade (30-60 cm) with parallel venation, scabrid (rough) margins, and prominent ligule and sickle-shaped auricles at junction of blade and sheath.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Grain enclosed in a yellowish-brown rough husk (lemma and palea) with ribbed surface; inside is an elongated oval polished or brown caryopsis grain.
season: Kharif (June-Nov), Rabi (Nov-April in Southern & Eastern India), Boro (Jan-May)
soil: Clayey loam, silty clay, or alluvial soils capable of holding standing water; pH 5.5-7.0
water: 1200-1500 mm total requirement; continuous 2-5 cm standing water from tillering to grain dough stage
seed_rate_and_sowing: Transplanting: 35-40 kg/ha (nursery sown 25-30 days before); DSR (Direct Seeded Rice): 20-25 kg/ha; Depth: 2-3 cm; Spacing: 20x15 cm
benefits: Primary calorie staple for over 60% of India
Easily digestible complex carbohydrates
Gluten-free energy source
Rice bran oil provides heart-healthy oryzanol
risks_or_cautions: High glycemic index in polished white rice poses blood glucose spikes for diabetics
Arsenic accumulation in soils with groundwater contamination
medicinal_uses: Rice gruel (kanji) used traditionally for rehydration in acute diarrhea
Ayurvedic Rakthashali red rice prescribed for tridosha balance

diseases.name: Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae)
diseases.symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical lesions with gray-white centers and dark brown margins on leaves; brown rot at panicle neck causing neck blast.
diseases.cause: Airborne fungus favoured by high humidity (>90%), night temp 19-23°C, and excessive nitrogen.
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of 5% Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE)
Pseudomonas fluorescens spray @ 10g/L or 2.5 kg/ha in water
prevention: Avoid excessive split doses of urea
Use resistant varieties like IR-64, Swarna Sub1
Seed treatment with Carbendazim 2g/kg

diseases.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked translucent stripes on leaf margins turning wavy yellow-white; bacterial ooze droplets drying into amber beads.
diseases.cause: Vascular bacterium entering via hydathodes or wounds, spread by flood irrigation and monsoon storms.
organic_treatment: Spray fresh cow dung water extract (20g/L)
Neem cake soil amendment @ 250 kg/ha
Copper hydroxide @ 2g/L
chemical_treatment_type: Streptocycline (90:10 streptomycin:tetracycline) 1g in 10L mixed with Copper Oxychloride 25g
prevention: Drain field for 3-4 days to arrest spread
Balanced potassium fertilization
Avoid clipping seedling tips during transplanting

diseases.name: Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani)
diseases.symptoms: Oval or greenish-gray water-soaked lesions on leaf sheath near water line, progressing into irregular spots with brown borders.
diseases.cause: Soil and water-borne sclerotia surviving between seasons; favoured by dense canopy and high humidity.
organic_treatment: Soil application of Trichoderma viride @ 2.5 kg/ha with FYM
Spray 3% neem oil with soap solution
prevention: Wider spacing (25x15 cm) to promote air flow
Avoid excess nitrogen
Deep summer ploughing to bury sclerotia

diseases.name: Yellow Stem Borer (Scirpophaga incertulas)
diseases.symptoms: Dead heart during vegetative phase (central shoot dies and pulls out easily); white earheads with chaffy grain at panicle stage.
diseases.cause: Lepidopteran moth larvae boring into leaf sheath and central stem tissue.
organic_treatment: Install pheromone traps with Helilure @ 12 traps/ha
Release Trichogramma japonicum egg parasitoid @ 100,000/ha weekly
Spray Neem oil 1500 ppm @ 3 ml/L
prevention: Clip off seedling tips before transplanting to remove egg masses
Collect and destroy stubble after harvest
Encourage spiders in canopy

diseases.name: Brown Planthopper (Nilaparvata lugens)
diseases.symptoms: Circular drying patches known as hopper burn; plants turn golden-brown, dry, and lodge; sooty mold develops on honey dew.
diseases.cause: Delphacid hopper sucking plant sap from base of tillers; favoured by heavy nitrogen and continuous flood.
organic_treatment: Drain standing water completely for 3-5 days to break cycle
Spray Metarhizium anisopliae @ 5g/L on basal stems
5% neem seed kernel extract
prevention: Provide ally ways of 30 cm after every 2-3 meters (skip row)
Do not spray synthetic pyrethroids which cause resurgence
Maintain alternate wetting and drying (AWD)

name: Wheat
how_to_identify_leaf: Flat, bluish-green linear leaves with parallel veins; prominent hairy auricles clasping the stem tightly at the base.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Spike terminal inflorescence with awns (beards) or awnless; oval kernels with a central ventral crease and apical brush of hairs.
season: Rabi (Sowing in Nov-Dec; Harvest in March-April)
soil: Well-drained fertile loamy to clayey loams; neutral pH 6.0-7.5; sensitive to salinity
water: 400-500 mm across 4-6 critical irrigations: CRI (21 DAS), Tillering, Late jointing, Flowering, Milk stage, Dough stage
seed_rate_and_sowing: Timely sown: 100 kg/ha; Late sown: 125 kg/ha; Row spacing 20-22.5 cm; Depth 4-5 cm (crucial not to sow deeper than 5 cm)
benefits: Primary source of protein and energy in North & Central India
Whole wheat bran supports digestive health
Provides sustained dietary fiber
risks_or_cautions: Contains gluten; strictly contraindicated for individuals with Celiac disease or gluten intolerance
medicinal_uses: Wheatgrass juice consumed traditionally for detoxification and immune support
Wheat bran decoction used for constipation relief

diseases.name: Yellow / Stripe Rust (Puccinia striiformis)
diseases.symptoms: Bright yellow powdery pustules arranged in prominent parallel stripes or ribbons on leaf blades and leaf sheaths.
diseases.cause: Airborne fungal spores favoured by cool humid conditions (10-15°C with morning dew), common in NW plains.
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of fermented cow urine + neem leaf extract (10%)
Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L
prevention: Sow rust-resistant cultivars like HD-2967, HD-3086, DBW-187, DBW-222
Avoid late November sowings
Eradicate alternate host barberry shrubs in hills

diseases.name: Brown / Leaf Rust (Puccinia triticina)
diseases.symptoms: Small, round to oval orange-brown powdery pustules scattered randomly across the upper leaf surface without forming stripes.
diseases.cause: Airborne urediniospores active in warmer temps (18-25°C) towards late January and February.
organic_treatment: Spray sour buttermilk solution (50 ml/L) mixed with copper sulfate (0.5g/L)
Neem oil 1500 ppm @ 3 ml/L
prevention: Timely sowing before Nov 20
Use resistant certified seeds
Destroy volunteer wheat plants

diseases.name: Karnal Bunt (Tilletia indica)
diseases.symptoms: Partial conversion of grain kernels into foul-smelling black powdery teliospore masses with fishy odor (trimethylamine).
diseases.cause: Soil and airborne fungus active during earhead emergence under cool, overcast, drizzly weather (15-20°C).
organic_treatment: Seed bio-priming with Trichoderma harzianum @ 10g/kg
Avoid flood irrigation during heading
chemical_treatment_type: Propiconazole 25% EC foliar spray at boot leaf/early flowering stage
prevention: Strict quarantine on seed movement
Rotate with non-host crops like mustard, gram or berseem
Deep summer ploughing

diseases.name: Loose Smut (Ustilago tritici)
diseases.symptoms: Entire earhead transformed into a loose sooty black mass of powdery spores leaving only the bare rachis at harvest.
diseases.cause: Internally seed-borne fungal mycelium dormant inside wheat embryo from previous season's infection.
organic_treatment: Solar heat treatment of seeds: soak in water for 4-5 hours in May, then dry on concrete in hot sun for 4 hours
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed only
Rogue out infected black earheads in polythene bags and burn

diseases.name: Wheat Aphid (Sitobion avenae / Rhopalosiphum padi)
diseases.symptoms: Clusters of small green or yellow insects on leaves, earheads and stems; honeydew secretion leads to black sooty mold; shriveled grains.
diseases.cause: Homopteran sap-sucking pest multiplying rapidly during warm cloudy spells in February-March.
organic_treatment: Conserve ladybird beetles (Coccinella septempunctata) and syrphid fly predators
Spray 5% NSKE or 3% Neem oil
prevention: Avoid excessive urea application which softens tissue
Timely sowing to escape peak aphid population in late winter

name: Maize
how_to_identify_leaf: Large, broad, strap-like sword-shaped leaves (50-100 cm long, 5-10 cm wide) with wavy margins, prominent white midrib, and alternate two-ranked arrangement.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Large cylindrical cob (ear) enclosed in tight fibrous husk, topped with silky tassels; rows of yellow, white, or orange hard kernels embedded on a central woody rachis.
season: Kharif (June-July), Rabi (Oct-Nov in Bihar/South), Spring (Jan-Feb in Punjab/Haryana)
soil: Deep, fertile, well-drained sandy loam to silty loam rich in organic matter; pH 6.0-7.5; cannot tolerate water stagnation
water: 500-750 mm; critical stages: Tasseling and Silking; sensitive to drought at flowering
seed_rate_and_sowing: Hybrids: 18-20 kg/ha; Sweet corn: 8-10 kg/ha; Fodder: 40-50 kg/ha; Spacing: 60x20 cm; Depth: 3-5 cm
benefits: Rich in lutein and zeaxanthin protecting retinal health
Energy-dense feed grain and staple food
Versatile industrial raw material (starch, corn oil, ethanol)
risks_or_cautions: High intake of unenriched maize without diverse protein can risk pellagra due to low tryptophan/niacin bioavailability
medicinal_uses: Corn silk (stigma maydis) brewed as a mild diuretic tea to support urinary tract and soothe bladder irritation

diseases.name: Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda)
diseases.symptoms: Ragged holes and severe skeletonization in whorl leaves; characteristic coarse sawdust-like fecal frass inside whorls; boring into cob.
diseases.cause: Invasive noctuid moth caterpillar with four black dots arranged in a square on 8th abdominal segment and inverted Y on head.
organic_treatment: Apply fine sand/soil + wood ash into central whorls (1:1 mix)
Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) kurstaki @ 2 g/L
Apply Metarhizium rileyi or Beauveria bassiana @ 5 g/L
prevention: Intercrop with pulses (cowpea, desmodium) in push-pull arrangement
Set up pheromone traps @ 10/ha at 10 days after germination
Deep ploughing in summer to expose pupae to birds

diseases.name: Maydis Leaf Blight (Bipolaris maydis)
diseases.symptoms: Small elongated diamond-shaped or oval brownish lesions with distinct margins on leaves, coalescing into extensive necrotic streaks.
diseases.cause: Ascomycete fungus favoured by warm, humid rainy weather (25-30°C and >80% RH).
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of 5% NSKE
Trichoderma viride spray @ 10 g/L
prevention: Use resistant hybrids like HQPM-1, Bio-9681
Destroy infected crop residues after harvest
Crop rotation with non-graminaceous crops

diseases.name: Turcicum Leaf Blight (Exserohilum turcicum)
diseases.symptoms: Large, long spindle-shaped or elliptical grayish-green or tan lesions (up to 15 cm long) starting on lower leaves and progressing upward.
diseases.cause: Fungus active in cool, moist weather (18-25°C) with morning fog and dew.
organic_treatment: Spray fresh buttermilk (50 ml/L) mixed with copper oxychloride (1.5 g/L)
Neem leaf decoction
prevention: Seed treatment with Thiram @ 3 g/kg
Maintain optimal plant spacing to avoid excessive leaf wetness

diseases.name: Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani f. sp. sasakii)
diseases.symptoms: Characteristic alternating dark brown and bleached straw-colored bands or zebra-stripes on leaf sheaths and leaves, reaching the cob.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne fungus spreading in warm humid conditions; sclerotia survive in soil.
organic_treatment: Strip off 2-3 lowest infected senescent leaves and sheaths
Pseudomonas fluorescens soil application
prevention: Avoid waterlogging around root base
Do not plant excessively dense populations
Seed treatment with Trichoderma

diseases.name: Maize Stem Borer (Chilo partellus)
diseases.symptoms: Pin-holes or 'shot holes' across leaves unfolding from whorl; dead heart in young plants; tunneling and frass inside the main stem.
diseases.cause: Crambid moth larva boring inside the stalk and whorl.
organic_treatment: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis @ 175,000/ha at 10-day intervals
Whorl application of neem seed powder mixed with sawdust
prevention: Pull and destroy dead heart plants
Sow maize as border crop with sorghum trap crops
Burn or compost maize stubble before spring

name: Tomato
how_to_identify_leaf: Compound pinnate leaves with 5-9 ovate to oblong leaflets; irregularly lobed, dentate edges, glandular hairs that emit a pungent green herbal odor when rubbed.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Fleshy globe, plum, or oblate berry with glossy red, orange, or yellow skin; multi-locular interior with slippery jelly surrounding small, flat, hairy teardrop-shaped buff seeds.
season: Autumn-Winter (sown Aug-Sept), Spring-Summer (sown Nov-Dec), Kharif (sown May-June)
soil: Well-drained sandy loam to clay loam rich in humus; pH 6.0-6.8; highly sensitive to waterlogging
water: 400-600 mm; regular drip irrigation; avoid overhead watering to prevent foliage disease; critical during fruit set
seed_rate_and_sowing: Hybrids: 100-150 g/ha; Open pollinated: 300-400 g/ha; Transplant 25-day seedlings at 60x45 cm or 75x60 cm spacing
benefits: Exceptional concentration of bioavailable lycopene for cardiovascular and prostate health
Rich source of vitamin C and antioxidants
Low-calorie dietary staple
risks_or_cautions: Leaves, stems, and unripe green fruits contain solanine and tomatine alkaloids toxic if ingested in large quantities
Acidity may irritate acid reflux sufferers
medicinal_uses: Dietary lycopene utilized for antioxidant and vascular endothelium support
Tomato pulp traditionally used as cooling topical astringent

diseases.name: Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
diseases.symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with concentric target-board rings on older lower leaves; yellow halos surround spots; defoliation moves upward.
diseases.cause: Fungus surviving in crop debris and solanaceous weeds; favoured by warm, humid weather with frequent rains (24-29°C).
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of 10% cow urine extract with garlic paste
Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L
Copper hydroxide @ 2 g/L
prevention: Prune bottom 12 inches of leaves to prevent soil splash
Mulch ground with straw or plastic
3-year crop rotation avoiding potato, brinjal, chilli

diseases.name: Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans)
diseases.symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked dark olive-brown patches on leaves with white fuzzy downy growth on leaf undersides in morning; rapid collapse.
diseases.cause: Oomycete pathogen thriving in cool, wet, foggy conditions (12-18°C and >90% RH).
organic_treatment: Bordeaux mixture 1% spray
Copper Oxychloride @ 3 g/L
prevention: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation
Ensure wide row spacing for canopy ventilation
Destroy all infected cull piles immediately

diseases.name: Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV)
diseases.symptoms: Severe upward and inward rolling/curling of leaves; thickening, leathery texture, yellowing margins; extreme stunting and complete flower drop.
diseases.cause: Begomovirus transmitted exclusively by the whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci).
organic_treatment: Install yellow sticky traps @ 25-30 traps/ha to monitor and trap whiteflies
Spray Neem oil (10,000 ppm) @ 2 ml/L or 5% NSKE regularly
Rogue out infected plants early
prevention: Use 40-mesh insect-proof nylon nets in nursery
Grow resistant hybrids (e.g., Arka Rakshak, Arka Abhed)
Grow border crops of maize or sorghum (3 rows)

diseases.name: Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum)
diseases.symptoms: Rapid daytime wilting of entire plant while leaves remain green; vascular browning in cut stem; white stream of bacterial ooze in clear water glass test.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne bacterium invading vascular system through root wounds; persists in soil for years.
organic_treatment: Soil drenching with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L
Bio-fumigation with mustard cover crop green manure
Bleaching powder @ 10-15 kg/ha applied before transplanting
chemical_treatment_type: Streptocycline 1 g + Copper Oxychloride 25 g in 10 L water drench around root zone
prevention: Plant resistant varieties like Arka Alok, Arka Abha
Avoid cultivating infested plots; maintain strict drainage
Graft scions onto bacterial wilt-resistant wild eggplant rootstock

diseases.name: Tomato Fruit Borer (Helicoverpa armigera)
diseases.symptoms: Circular entrance holes on developing fruits with the caterpillar's rear portion protruding outside; fruit rotting and falling prematurely.
diseases.cause: Polyphagous moth whose larvae feed on flower buds and bore into green or ripening fruits.
organic_treatment: Plant African marigold (Tagetes erecta) as trap crop (1 row marigold for every 16 rows tomato)
Spray HaNPV (Helicoverpa nuclear polyhedrosis virus) @ 250 LE/ha with 0.5% jaggery
Pheromone traps with Helilure @ 10/ha
prevention: Hand-pick and destroy early instar larvae on leaves and flowers
Deep summer ploughing to destroy pupae in soil

name: Potato
how_to_identify_leaf: Interruptedly pinnate compound leaves with 3-4 pairs of large ovate leaflets interspersed with tiny interjected leaflets; pubescent with slightly wavy margins.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Swollen underground stem tuber with shallow 'eyes' (buds) scattered spirally; skin buff, brown, red, or purple; flesh white, cream, or yellow.
season: Rabi in plains (Oct-Nov to Jan-Feb); Summer in hills (March-April to Aug-Sept)
soil: Loose, well-aerated sandy loam rich in organic matter; pH 5.2-6.5; heavy clay hinders tuber enlargement and causes deformities
water: 450-550 mm; frequent light irrigations; stop watering 10-14 days before harvest to harden tuber skin
seed_rate_and_sowing: Whole seed tubers (30-40g size) with 2-3 active sprouts: 2.5-3.0 tonnes/ha; Spacing: 60x20 cm; Depth: 7-10 cm in ridges and furrows
benefits: Highly bioavailable potassium supporting electrolyte and blood pressure balance
Resistant starch formed when cooked and cooled aids gut microbiome
Accessible, filling culinary staple
risks_or_cautions: Green skin areas exposed to light contain solanine and chaconine glycoalkaloids; discard green potatoes to avoid poisoning
medicinal_uses: Raw potato slices applied topically to calm minor skin burns and soothe sun-irritated skin
Potato juice traditionally consumed for mild peptic acidity

diseases.name: Late Blight of Potato (Phytophthora infestans)
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked irregular brown lesions on leaf tips/margins with white mildew under leaf in high humidity; tuber flesh develops dry rust-brown granular rot.
diseases.cause: Oomycete pathogen surviving in infected seed tubers; explodes during cool overcast weather (12-20°C and >85% RH).
organic_treatment: Prophylactic spray of Bordeaux mixture 1%
Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride @ 3 g/L
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers from cold store
High earthing up to prevent zoospores from washing down to tubers
Dehaulming (cutting off haulms) 10 days before harvest

diseases.name: Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
diseases.symptoms: Brown to black spots with concentric rings ('target board' pattern) on older lower leaves, causing premature yellowing and drying.
diseases.cause: Airborne fungal conidia active in alternating wet and dry periods (25-30°C).
organic_treatment: Spray neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 2 ml/L
Trichoderma viride foliar spray @ 5 g/L
prevention: Avoid water stress and maintain balanced fertility
Destroy infected haulms post-harvest

diseases.name: Common Scab (Streptomyces scabies)
diseases.symptoms: Rough, corky, raised or pitted brown pustules on tuber skin; reduces commercial grade though inner flesh remains edible.
diseases.cause: Soil actinomycete surviving indefinitely in dry, alkaline soils (pH > 6.5).
organic_treatment: Green manuring with sunn hemp before potato crop
Soil application of elemental sulfur to lower pH below 5.5
Seed treatment with Trichoderma
chemical_treatment_type: Seed tuber dip in Boric acid 3% solution for 30 minutes before storage or planting
prevention: Maintain adequate soil moisture during tuber initiation for 4-6 weeks
Avoid applying fresh uncomposted lime or poultry manure

diseases.name: Potato Tuber Moth (Phthorimaea operculella)
diseases.symptoms: Mined blotches and galleries in leaves; larvae bore deep tunnels into tubers in field and store packed with dark silken excrement.
diseases.cause: Microlepidopteran moth laying eggs on exposed tubers or foliage; active in warm storage conditions.
organic_treatment: Cover tubers in country stores with 2.5 cm layer of dried Lantana camara or eucalyptus leaves
Pheromone traps in stores
chemical_treatment_type: Spray Quinalphos 25% EC @ 2 ml/L in field before earthing up
Bt kurstaki dust on seed tubers
prevention: Deep planting and compact earthing up so tubers are never exposed
Prompt harvest without leaving harvested bags overnight in field

diseases.name: Potato Apical Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCNDV-potato)
diseases.symptoms: Severe curling, crinkling, and mosaic of top leaves with conspicuous yellowing; pronounced stunting of plant.
diseases.cause: Geminivirus transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci); rampant in early sown crop in Northern plains.
organic_treatment: Yellow sticky traps @ 25/ha
Neem formulation sprays (10,000 ppm) @ 2 ml/L
chemical_treatment_type: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL seed tuber spray before planting
prevention: Adjust planting date to mid-October after whitefly vector population drops
Use vector-free certified foundation seed

name: Brinjal
how_to_identify_leaf: Large, alternate, ovate to oblong leaves with shallowly lobed or sinuate margins; star-shaped (stellate) hairs on surface; some varieties bear sharp spines on midrib.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Fleshy pendant berry, glossy purple, green, striped or white; shape oblong, teardrop or spherical; interior soft spongy white flesh containing numerous tiny flat kidney-shaped pale seeds.
season: Autumn-Winter crop (sown June-July), Spring-Summer crop (sown Nov-Dec), Summer crop (sown Feb-March)
soil: Deep, fertile silt loam or clay loam with high organic content; well drained; pH 6.0-6.8
water: 600-800 mm; requires consistent moisture; irrigate every 4-6 days during summer, 8-10 days in winter
seed_rate_and_sowing: Hybrids: 150-200 g/ha; Varieties: 350-400 g/ha; Transplant 30-35 day seedlings at 75x60 cm or 90x60 cm spacing
benefits: Nasunin anthocyanin in purple skin is a potent antioxidant protecting cellular brain membranes
High dietary fiber helps manage cholesterol absorption
Low calorie food suitable for weight control
risks_or_cautions: Contains moderate oxalates; individuals with history of calcium oxalate kidney stones should consume in moderation
May trigger oral itching in people with nightshade sensitivity
medicinal_uses: Roasted brinjal pulp consumed in traditional folk diets for liver health
Decoction of brinjal roots traditionally used for soothing respiratory distress

diseases.name: Shoot and Fruit Borer (Leucinodes orbonalis)
diseases.symptoms: Wilting and drooping of tender growing shoot tips; small entry holes on fruits plugged with chewed frass; rotting inside fruit.
diseases.cause: Pyralid moth whose pinkish larvae bore inside shoots in vegetative phase and into fruits during fruiting.
organic_treatment: Clip and destroy wilted shoots along with larvae weekly
Install Lucilure pheromone traps @ 25-30/ha
Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 2 g/L
Neem seed kernel extract 5%
prevention: Intercrop with coriander or fennel to encourage beneficial parasitoids
Rogue out and bury damaged fruits deep in soil
Avoid continuous brinjal cultivation

diseases.name: Little Leaf of Brinjal
diseases.symptoms: Extreme reduction in leaf size forming tiny, clustered, bush-like malformed leaves; excessive bushiness (witches' broom); plant bears no fruit.
diseases.cause: Phytoplasma organism transmitted by leafhopper vector (Hishimonus phycitis).
organic_treatment: Rogue and burn infected plants immediately on first appearance
Spray neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 2 ml/L against leafhoppers
chemical_treatment_type: Oxytetracycline hydrochloride foliar spray (temporarily suppresses symptoms)
prevention: Dip seedlings in Tetracycline solution (500 ppm) for 30 minutes before transplanting
Keep field edges clear of wild solanaceous weed hosts

diseases.name: Phomopsis Blight (Phomopsis vexans)
diseases.symptoms: Circular brown leaf spots with pale centers turning paper-thin; soft, watery, pale brown sunken spots on fruit covered with black pycnidia pimples.
diseases.cause: Seed and soil-borne fungus spreading rapidly during warm rainy seasons (28-32°C).
organic_treatment: Hot water seed treatment at 50°C for 30 minutes
Spray copper oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds
Follow crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops
Collect and burn fallen diseased fruits

diseases.name: Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum)
diseases.symptoms: Sudden drop and wilting of whole foliage during warm afternoons while leaves stay green; vascular ring turns dark brown; milky ooze in clear water.
diseases.cause: Bacterium surviving in soil and water channels, entering through nematode or root injury.
organic_treatment: Soil drenching with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L
Crop rotation with non-hosts like maize or rice
Amend soil with neem cake
chemical_treatment_type: Drenching with Streptocycline 1g + Copper Oxychloride 25g per 10 L water
prevention: Plant resistant varieties (e.g., Pant Rituraj, Arka Nidhi, Pusa Purple Cluster)
Control root-knot nematodes which create entry points

diseases.name: Two-Spotted Spider Mite (Tetranychus urticae)
diseases.symptoms: Tiny white or yellow stipples on upper leaf surface; fine silken webbing on leaf undersides; leaves turn bronzed, dusty and dry up.
diseases.cause: Acarine pest multiplying massively in hot, dry, dusty weather (>30°C and low RH).
organic_treatment: Forceful water spray on leaf undersides to dislodge webbing
Spray wettable sulfur 80% WDG @ 3 g/L
Neem oil 1500 ppm @ 3 ml/L
prevention: Avoid dusty roadside locations without shelterbelts
Do not overuse broad-spectrum synthetic pyrethroids which kill predatory mites

name: Chilli
how_to_identify_leaf: Simple, alternate or paired, lanceolate to elliptic-ovate leaves with acute apex, entire margins, glossy dark green surface with smooth texture.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Elongated, conical, or slender glossy pod berry; green turning fiery red, orange, or yellow when ripe; filled with pungent placenta bearing flat disc-shaped yellowish seeds.
season: Kharif (sown May-June), Rabi (sown Sept-Oct), Summer (sown Jan-Feb in irrigated tracts)
soil: Well-drained light loamy soils rich in organic matter; pH 6.0-7.0; cannot tolerate water stagnation even for 24 hours
water: 500-600 mm; sensitive to excess moisture; light, frequent irrigation (drip irrigation preferred)
seed_rate_and_sowing: Hybrids: 200-250 g/ha; Varieties: 1.0 kg/ha; Nursery raised 30 days; Spacing: 60x45 cm or 75x45 cm
benefits: Capsaicin boosts metabolic rate and thermogenesis
Extremely dense natural source of vitamin C and carotenoids
Stimulates gastric secretions and circulation
risks_or_cautions: Capsaicin irritates mucous membranes and eyes; excessive consumption can exacerbate gastric ulcers and acid reflux
medicinal_uses: Topical capsaicin formulations used clinically for neuropathic pain and osteoarthritis analgesia
Counter-irritant in traditional liniments

diseases.name: Chilli Leaf Curl Virus (ChiLCV)
diseases.symptoms: Upward curling and puckering of leaves with boat-shaped deformity; shortening of internodes resulting in severe stunting; no fruit formation.
diseases.cause: Begomovirus transmitted by the whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci).
organic_treatment: Install yellow sticky cards @ 30/ha
Foliar spray of 5% NSKE or Neem oil (10,000 ppm) @ 2 ml/L
Rogue out infected plants early
prevention: Raise seedlings under 40-mesh insect netting
Barrier crops of 3 rows of maize around the field
Grow resistant hybrids like Arka Gagan, Arka Kyati

diseases.name: Anthracnose / Dieback (Colletotrichum capsici)
diseases.symptoms: Tips of branches die backward turning white and dry (dieback); circular sunken spots with concentric rings of black dots on ripening fruits (fruit rot).
diseases.cause: Seed and air-borne fungus favoured by high humidity (>80%) and temperatures around 28°C during fruit ripening.
organic_treatment: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 10 g/kg
Spray Bordeaux mixture 1% or Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L
prevention: Use disease-free seed from healthy fruits
Avoid sprinkler overhead irrigation
Remove and burn infected twigs and fruits

diseases.name: Chilli Thrips (Scirtothrips dorsalis)
diseases.symptoms: Leaves curl upward from margins; silvery bronze or brown rust-like streaks on underside; brittle leaves; stunted crinkled shoots.
diseases.cause: Slender yellow microscopic thrips feeding on tender sap, active in dry warm weather.
organic_treatment: Install blue sticky traps @ 25/ha (thrips are attracted to blue)
Spray spinosad-derived organic formulations or neem oil
Spray Lecanicillium lecanii @ 5 g/L
prevention: Sprinkle water on crop canopy in morning to knock down thrips
Avoid planting near old cotton or onion fields

diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Leveillula taurica)
diseases.symptoms: White powdery patches on underside of leaves with corresponding yellow chlorotic lesions on upper surface; heavy defoliation.
diseases.cause: Endophytic fungus active in warm, dry weather with high morning humidity.
organic_treatment: Spray wettable sulfur 80% WDG @ 3 g/L
Spray milk and water mix (1:9) on foliage in bright sun
prevention: Maintain wide plant spacing
Spray sulfur prophylactically when dry warm weather sets in

diseases.name: Damping Off (Pythium aphanidermatum)
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on seedling collar region at soil line; seedlings topple over and rot in nursery beds within 48 hours.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne oomycete pathogen favoured by heavy seed beds, excess water, and poor drainage.
organic_treatment: Soil solarization of nursery beds with clear polythene sheets for 4 weeks in May
Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum @ 10 g/kg
chemical_treatment_type: Seed treatment with Metalaxyl 35% WS @ 3 g/kg
Soil drenching with Copper Oxychloride @ 3 g/L
prevention: Always prepare raised nursery beds (15 cm high)
Avoid dense sowing of seed in nursery

name: Onion
how_to_identify_leaf: Hollow, cylindrical, glaucous bluish-green tubular leaves (fistular) with pointed tips, flattened on the inner side, emerging from a basal bulb neck.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Layered underground tunicated bulb with dry papery outer scales (red, yellow, or white); small angular jet-black wrinkled seeds produced on spherical umbels.
season: Kharif (sown May-June), Late Kharif (Aug-Sept), Rabi (Oct-Nov; represents 60% of India's output)
soil: Friable, fertile sandy loam to light clay loam rich in organic matter; free from stones; pH 6.5-7.5; very sensitive to waterlogging
water: 350-550 mm; shallow root system demands frequent light irrigations (every 5-7 days in summer); withhold water 15 days before harvest
seed_rate_and_sowing: 8-10 kg/ha for seedlings; Nursery transplanting at 6-8 weeks old; Spacing: 15x10 cm on flat beds or raised beds
benefits: Exceptional concentration of quercetin flavonoid for heart health and anti-inflammatory activity
Organosulfur compounds help lower blood pressure and platelet aggregation
Prebiotic inulin supports healthy gut bacteria
risks_or_cautions: Contains fermentable oligo-saccharides (FODMAPs) which may trigger bloating in IBS sufferers
Toxic to dogs and cats due to thiosulfate content
medicinal_uses: Fresh onion juice used traditionally as ear drop for mild earache and topical insect bite relief
Crushed onion inhalation used as folk remedy for congestion

diseases.name: Purple Blotch (Alternaria porri)
diseases.symptoms: Small water-soaked sunken lesions on leaves and seed stalks developing purple or dark centers with broad yellow halos, causing leaves to break over.
diseases.cause: Fungus favored by warm, humid rainy weather (21-30°C and 80-90% RH).
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of 5% NSKE mixed with adhesive sticker
Spray Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L
prevention: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation
Use disease-free sets and certified seeds
Dip seedlings in Mancozeb (2g/L) for 15 minutes before transplanting

diseases.name: Onion Thrips (Thrips tabaci)
diseases.symptoms: Silvery patches and white blotches on leaves caused by rasping-sucking feeding; leaves curl, turn brown, and wither from tip downwards.
diseases.cause: Tiny yellowish-brown thrips hiding in inner leaf sheaths, multiplying rapidly during hot dry spells.
organic_treatment: Install blue sticky traps @ 25/ha
Spray 3% neem oil with mild detergent as wetting agent
Spray Beauveria bassiana @ 5 g/L
prevention: Maintain border crop of two rows of maize or barrier netting
Sprinkler irrigation helps wash thrips off tubular foliage

diseases.name: Stemphylium Leaf Blight (Stemphylium vesicarium)
diseases.symptoms: Small yellow to pale orange oval spots on leaves, rapidly expanding into elongated dark olive-brown patches covered with black soot-like conidia.
diseases.cause: Fungus active in warm humid conditions; commonly follows thrips injury or purple blotch infection.
organic_treatment: Spray Bordeaux mixture 1%
Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L
prevention: Control thrips early as wounds promote entry
Ensure proper balanced potassium fertilization

diseases.name: Basal Rot / Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cepae)
diseases.symptoms: Progressive yellowing and dying back of leaves from tip; roots rot and turn pinkish-brown; bulb base becomes soft, decayed and watery.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne pathogen entering through root wounds or basal plate, active in warm soil (>28°C).
organic_treatment: Seedling root dip in Trichoderma viride @ 10 g/L for 30 minutes
Apply Trichoderma enriched FYM @ 5 tonnes/ha to soil
chemical_treatment_type: Carbendazim 50% WP root dip @ 1 g/L and soil drenching
prevention: Follow 4-year crop rotation with non-allium crops
Avoid mechanical damage to roots and bulbs during weeding

diseases.name: Downy Mildew (Peronospora destructor)
diseases.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow oval patches on leaves covered with violet-gray fuzzy down in moist mornings; leaves collapse and dry up.
diseases.cause: Oomycete favored by cool, foggy, humid nights followed by mild days.
organic_treatment: Prophylactic spray of Copper Hydroxide @ 2 g/L
Avoid dense seedling stands
prevention: Proper spacing to allow wind circulation
Avoid planting downwind of old infected onion fields

name: Mango
how_to_identify_leaf: Simple, alternate, oblong-lanceolate leathery evergreen leaves (15-30 cm); tender new leaves copper-red or pinkish, turning dark glossy green with prominent light green veins; aromatic resinous odor when crushed.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Large fleshy asymmetric drupe with smooth skin (green turning golden-yellow or flushed with red); juicy orange-yellow sweet flesh enclosing a large flat fibrous woody endocarp stone.
lookalikes: Neem leaf (pinnate compound, vs mango simple)
season: Flowering in Dec-Feb; Fruit harvest in March-July depending on zone
soil: Deep, well-drained alluvial or red loamy soil with minimum 2m root depth; pH 5.5-7.5; water table below 2.5m
water: Rainfed in high rainfall regions; 2-3 irrigations between fruit set and maturity dramatically increases fruit size; withhold irrigation 2 months prior to flowering
seed_rate_and_sowing: Propagated vegetatively via epicotyl/wedge grafting onto local rootstocks; Spacing: 10x10 m (traditional) or 5x5 m (High Density Planting); Planting in monsoon
benefits: Mangiferin polyphenol provides powerful antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity
High beta-carotene and vitamin A promote visual and skin health
Rich enzymes aid digestive processes
risks_or_cautions: Sap and skin contains urushiol traces which can cause contact dermatitis ('mango mouth') in sensitive people
High fructose requires portion management in diabetic diets
medicinal_uses: Tender mango leaves brewed into decoction traditionally in Ayurveda to manage blood sugar
Dried mango seed kernel powder (Amchur/gutka) used for diarrhea and intestinal worms

diseases.name: Anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides)
diseases.symptoms: Dark brown to black sunken circular spots with tear-stain patterns on leaves, blossoms, and fruits; blossom blight causes complete flower drop.
diseases.cause: Fungus thriving during warm, misty, rainy weather during flowering and fruit development.
organic_treatment: Prune dead twigs and spray 1% Bordeaux mixture before flowering
Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L
prevention: Post-harvest hot water treatment of fruits at 52°C for 5 minutes
Prune inner branches to open canopy to sunlight

diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Oidium mangiferae)
diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth covering panicles, flowers, and tiny fruitlets; causes total fruitlet dropping and floral mummification.
diseases.cause: Airborne spores favoured by cool nights and warm dry days with cloudy morning weather in Dec-Feb.
organic_treatment: Dusting sulfur powder @ 350 mesh or spray Wettable Sulfur 80% WDG @ 3 g/L
Spray potassium bicarbonate @ 5 g/L
prevention: First spray at panicle emergence, second at full bloom, third at pea-stage

diseases.name: Mango Hopper (Idioscopus clypealis / Amritodus atkinsoni)
diseases.symptoms: Wedge-shaped tiny hoppers suck sap from tender panicles and leaves; panicles turn brown and dry; copious sticky honeydew causes heavy sooty mold.
diseases.cause: Cicadellid insect multiplying in hundreds on mango panicles during flowering season.
organic_treatment: Spray 5% NSKE at panicle emergence
Spray Beauveria bassiana @ 5 g/L on tree trunk and branches where adults hide
Neem oil 1500 ppm @ 3 ml/L
prevention: Prune dense criss-cross branches to allow sunlight into interior canopy
Avoid spraying chemicals during peak pollinator bee activity hours (morning)

diseases.name: Mango Fruit Fly (Bactrocera dorsalis)
diseases.symptoms: Punctures with brown resinous oozing on maturing fruit skin; white maggots feed inside pulp causing soft, foul-smelling rotting and premature drop.
diseases.cause: Tephritid fly inserting eggs below fruit epidermis during fruit maturity (April-June).
organic_treatment: Install Methyl Eugenol pheromone traps @ 10 traps/ha from fruit marble stage
Bait spray: Jaggery 100g + Malathion 10ml in 10L water on lower canopy
chemical_treatment_type: Spray Deltamethrin 2.8% EC @ 1 ml/L (respect harvest waiting period of 7 days)
prevention: Collect and bury fallen infested fruits at least 2 feet underground
Plough tree basin in summer to expose pupae to predatory ants and birds

diseases.name: Mango Malformation (Fusarium mangiferae)
diseases.symptoms: Vegetative malformation: bunchy compact shoots with tiny leaves ('bunchy top'); Floral malformation: compact, thick, hypertrophied panicles without fruit setting.
diseases.cause: Fungal pathogen transmitted and aggravated by the mango bud mite (Aceria mangiferae).
organic_treatment: Prune and burn malformed panicles along with 15 cm of healthy wood below the cluster
Spray neem oil on buds
chemical_treatment_type: Spray NAA (Naphthalene Acetic Acid) @ 200 ppm in October
Acaricide spray (Dicofol or Wettable sulfur) to control bud mite
prevention: Sterilize pruning shears with ethanol between cuts
Use disease-free scion wood for grafting

name: Banana
how_to_identify_leaf: Giant, spirally arranged, oblong paddle-shaped leaves (up to 2-3 m long, 60 cm wide) with thick central midrib, parallel lateral veins, easily tearing along veins in wind.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Hanging bunch consisting of tiers ('hands') of elongated, slightly curved, cylindrical berries with thick yellow or green peel and creamy seedless pulp; large pendant purple terminal bud.
season: Planted year-round in South/Coastal India; peak harvest 11-13 months after planting
soil: Deep, fertile, well-drained loamy soil with rich humus; pH 6.0-7.5; water table below 1m; highly sensitive to poor drainage and salinity
water: 1800-2200 mm; high water demand; requires 15-20 liters/plant/day through drip irrigation; sensitive to drought at flowering
seed_rate_and_sowing: Propagated via sword suckers (1.5-2.0 kg) or tissue culture plantlets; Population: 2500-3000 plants/ha; Spacing: 1.8x1.8 m or 1.5x1.5 m
benefits: Rapid natural carbohydrate energy release ideal for physical recovery
Rich potassium helps regulate blood pressure and counter sodium
Vitamin B6 supports neurotransmitter synthesis
risks_or_cautions: High glycemic index in overripe bananas warrants moderation in strict diabetic diets
High potassium intake caution for advanced renal failure patients
medicinal_uses: Banana stem juice consumed traditionally for renal calculi (kidney stone) dissolution
Raw green banana flour utilized for resistant starch gut healing

diseases.name: Panama Wilt / Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense - TR4 & race 1)
diseases.symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaf margins progressing inward; leaves buckle at petiole and hang down forming a skirt around pseudostem; reddish-brown vascular discolouration inside stem.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne chlamydospores persisting for 30+ years; TR4 affects Cavendish clones; spreads via infected suckers and running water.
organic_treatment: Soil application of bioagent Trichoderma viride / harzianum @ 50g/plant with 5 kg neem cake
Drench with Pseudomonas fluorescens
chemical_treatment_type: Capsule application of 2,4-D or glyphosate to kill infected mats; no chemical cure exists once infected
prevention: Strict quarantine on suckers; use certified tissue-culture plantlets only
Dip suckers in Carbendazim 2g/L before planting
Crop rotation with paddy or sugarcane

diseases.name: Sigatoka Leaf Spot (Pseudocercospora fijiensis / musicola)
diseases.symptoms: Small yellowish streaks parallel to leaf veins turning dark reddish-brown with sunken gray centers and yellow halos; extensive leaf death.
diseases.cause: Ascomycete fungus spread by rain splash and wind in warm, rainy, humid tropical conditions.
organic_treatment: Deleafing: cut and burn severely infected leaf strips
Foliar spray of mineral oil / petroleum spray oil @ 10 ml/L
Bordeaux mixture 1%
prevention: Maintain efficient drainage channels to reduce canopy humidity
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation
Maintain proper spacing

diseases.name: Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV)
diseases.symptoms: Dark green 'Morse-code' dots and dashes along secondary leaf veins and petiole; leaves become upright, narrow, brittle, and crowded in a rosette bunch at the crown; zero bunch production.
diseases.cause: Nanovirus transmitted by the banana black aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa).
organic_treatment: Inject infected pseudostem with kerosene or 2,4-D to kill plant
Spray 3% neem oil on aphids around leaf axils
chemical_treatment_type: Vector control: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 ml/L directed into leaf axils and base of suckers
prevention: Never source suckers from areas where bunchy top exists
Rogue out and destroy infected mats immediately to prevent vector spread

diseases.name: Pseudostem Weevil / Borer (Odoiporus longicollis)
diseases.symptoms: Pin-head sized holes on pseudostem with transparent jelly-like resin oozing out; rotting internal stem tissue leading to snapping and lodging in wind.
diseases.cause: Curculionid weevil larva tunneling extensively inside the false stem.
organic_treatment: Install split pseudostem longitudinal traps @ 60-70 traps/ha smeared with Beauveria bassiana
Cosmopolites pheromone traps
chemical_treatment_type: Pseudostem injection of Monocrotophos / Chlorpyrifos @ 1 ml/plant
Stem swabbing with Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 2.5 ml/L
prevention: Clean cultivation; remove dry hanging leaf sheaths periodically
Chop and destroy harvested pseudostems down to rhizome level

diseases.name: Banana Rhizome Weevil (Cosmopolites sordidus)
diseases.symptoms: Larvae tunnel throughout the corm/rhizome, riddling it with blackened galleries; roots decay; plants are easily blown over by mild breeze.
diseases.cause: Weevil active in moist soil and decaying plant debris around the corm.
organic_treatment: Sucker paring (trimming outer tissue) and pralinage: dip sucker in mud slurry mixed with neem cake powder
Apply Beauveria bassiana to sucker basin
chemical_treatment_type: Carbofuran 3% G @ 20g per sucker placed in planting pit
prevention: Select healthy suckers free from black tunnel marks
Hot water treatment of suckers at 50°C for 20 minutes before planting

name: Papaya
how_to_identify_leaf: Large, palmately 7-9 lobed deeply cut leaves (50-70 cm wide) on long hollow petioles (up to 1 m), radiating spirally from the crown top of an unbranched soft-wood trunk.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Large oval, oblong, or pear-shaped melon-like berry with thin green skin turning yellow-orange; orange-red soft flesh with sweet musky taste and large central cavity filled with black peppery mucilaginous seeds.
season: Planted in Monsoon (June-July) or Spring (Feb-March); fruits harvested 9-10 months later
soil: Well-drained rich sandy loam with high organic matter; highly vulnerable to collar rot in heavy clay; pH 6.0-6.8
water: Regular moderate irrigation; strictly cannot tolerate standing water around trunk even for a few hours (causes collar rot); drip irrigation ideal
seed_rate_and_sowing: 500 g/ha (varieties) or 100-150 g/ha (gynodioecious hybrids like Red Lady 786); Transplant 45-day seedlings at 2.0x2.0 m or 1.8x1.8 m
benefits: Papain proteolytic enzyme supports digestion and alleviates functional dyspepsia
Exceptionally high natural vitamin C and beta-carotene content
Carica papaya leaf extract widely researched for increasing platelet count during dengue fever
risks_or_cautions: Unripe or semi-ripe green papaya contains high latex concentrations that stimulate uterine contractions; contraindicated in pregnancy
Can provoke latex-fruit allergy cross-reactions
medicinal_uses: Fresh green papaya leaf juice decoction used traditionally to support thrombocyte (platelet) recovery in dengue
Crushed black seeds used in folk medicine for intestinal parasites

diseases.name: Papaya Ringspot Virus (PRSV)
diseases.symptoms: Yellow mosaic and vein clearing on leaves; intense blistering and reduction of leaf blade ('shoestring' effect); dark green oily water-soaked rings on fruit and green streaks on petiole.
diseases.cause: Potyvirus transmitted non-persistently by various aphid species (Aphis gossypii, Myzus persicae).
organic_treatment: Spray 2% neem oil or 5% NSKE to deter aphids
Rogue out infected plants immediately to reduce field inoculum
chemical_treatment_type: Vector suppression: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L
prevention: Raise seedlings under insect-proof net house
Intercrop with barrier rows of maize, sorghum or sesbania
Avoid planting near cucurbits (squash, cucumber, watermelon) which host the virus

diseases.name: Stem / Foot Rot / Damping Off (Pythium aphanidermatum / Phytophthora palmivora)
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on trunk base near soil line; stem softens and rots spongy-brown; tree easily topples over during wind.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne oomycete pathogen exploding in poorly drained waterlogged soils during heavy monsoon rains.
organic_treatment: Scrape rotten bark and apply Bordeaux paste (1:1:10) to the stem base
Soil application of Trichoderma viride @ 50g/tree with FYM
chemical_treatment_type: Soil drenching around stem with Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L
prevention: Plant on raised mounds (30-40 cm high)
Ensure slope drainage prevents water contact with trunk base
Never allow irrigation water to touch the stem bark

diseases.name: Papaya Leaf Curl Virus (PaLCuV)
diseases.symptoms: Severe downward rolling and curling of leaves; thickened leathery veins with vein enations (ruffled crests); severely stunted plants with deformed fruits.
diseases.cause: Begomovirus transmitted by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).
organic_treatment: Yellow sticky traps @ 30/ha
Neem formulation (10,000 ppm) @ 2 ml/L spray every 10 days
prevention: Destroy solanaceous weed hosts (Solanum nigrum, Datura) in surrounding borders
Rogue out early diseased trees

diseases.name: Anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides)
diseases.symptoms: Small round water-soaked spots on ripening fruits expanding into circular sunken dark lesions with pinkish spore masses; internal pulp decays.
diseases.cause: Fungus latent in fruit tissues from flowering, developing rapidly as sugars increase during ripening.
organic_treatment: Hot water dip of harvested fruits at 48°C for 20 minutes
Spray Copper Hydroxide @ 2 g/L on developing fruits
prevention: Spray fruit bunches periodically during rainy periods
Handle fruits with clean gloves during harvest to prevent skin abrasions

diseases.name: Papaya Mealybug (Paracoccus marginatus)
diseases.symptoms: Clusters of small, soft, oval insects covered with white waxy mealy powder on undersides of leaves, fruits and stems; crinkled deformed leaves covered with black sooty mold.
diseases.cause: Invasive pseudococcid bug multiplying rapidly in warm dry weather; attended by ants.
organic_treatment: Release classical biological control parasitoid Acerophagus papayae (dramatically successful across India)
Spray Neem oil 2% mixed with 0.5% liquid soap to strip wax
Spray Verticillium lecanii @ 5 g/L
prevention: Destroy ant nests around tree base
Prune and burn heavily encrusted leaves
Avoid broad spectrum sprays that kill Acerophagus parasitoids

name: Guava
how_to_identify_leaf: Opposite, simple, elliptic to oblong leaves (7-15 cm) with prominent parallel veins depressed on upper surface and raised beneath; short petiole, aromatic aroma when crushed.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Round, oval, or pyriform fleshy berry crowned by persistent calyx lobes; thin pale green to yellowish skin; white, pink, or red aromatic flesh studded with numerous small hard bony seeds.
season: Bahar treatment determines crop: Mrig Bahar (harvest in winter: Nov-Jan, highest quality); Ambe Bahar (harvest in rainy season: July-Aug)
soil: Highly adaptable; grows from sandy to clay soils; tolerates pH from 5.5 to 8.5; tolerates moderate salinity and alkalinity
water: Rainfed in high rainfall regions; 6-8 irrigations during fruit growth; withhold irrigation for 2 months to induce flowering (Bahar regulation)
seed_rate_and_sowing: Propagated by air-layering (guthi) or wedge grafting; Spacing: 6x6 m (traditional) or 3x3 m (Meadow orchard system); Planting in July-August
benefits: Unrivaled natural vitamin C density (over 4 times higher than orange)
High soluble dietary pectin fiber supports glycemic control and healthy digestion
Rich in lycopene and polyphenols
risks_or_cautions: Hard seeds may pose discomfort for diverticulosis sufferers; chew thoroughly
Overeating unripe guava may cause constipation due to high astringent tannin content
medicinal_uses: Tender guava leaf decoction widely used as antimicrobial mouth rinse for gingivitis and oral ulcers
Leaf tea used in traditional medicine for acute watery diarrhea

diseases.name: Guava Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. psidii)
diseases.symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of leaves starting on one branch and spreading to whole tree; leaves dry up and hang; internal xylem vessels turn dark brownish-purple.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne vascular fungus favored by alkaline soils (pH > 7.5) and high summer heat; enter roots damaged by nematodes.
organic_treatment: Soil application of Trichoderma viride @ 50g mixed with 5 kg neem cake per tree basin
Maintain soil pH around 6.5 with organic amendments
chemical_treatment_type: Drenching tree basin with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L
prevention: Graft scions onto wilt-resistant rootstock Psidium friedrichsthalianum (Chinese guava)
Avoid cultivating roots during weeding

diseases.name: Fruit Fly (Bactrocera correcta / B. dorsalis)
diseases.symptoms: Oviposition puncture marks with rotting and brown discoloration; internal pulp riddled with wriggling white larvae; premature fruit drop.
diseases.cause: Tephritid fly laying eggs under fruit skin, rampant during monsoon (Ambe Bahar crop).
organic_treatment: Bagging individual fruits with non-woven paper/polythene bags when marble sized (100% protection)
Install Methyl Eugenol pheromone traps @ 15/ha
chemical_treatment_type: Bait spray: Protein hydrolysate / Jaggery 100g + Malathion 50% EC 10ml in 10L water
prevention: Harvest fruits at firm mature-green stage before ripening on tree
Deep ploughing in tree basins to expose puparia

diseases.name: Anthracnose / Dieback (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides)
diseases.symptoms: Shoots die back from top downward; small pin-point circular dark brown sunken spots on fruit that enlarge and coalesce into dark scabby patches.
diseases.cause: Fungus spreading through rain splashes in warm humid weather during July-September.
organic_treatment: Prune dead twigs 5 cm below infected area and apply copper paste
Bordeaux mixture 1% spray
prevention: Prune internal dense canopy for ventilation
Disinfect pruning secateurs

diseases.name: Canker (Pestalotiopsis psidii)
diseases.symptoms: Small brown angular necrotic spots on leaves; on green fruits, circular raised corky pustules with ruptured epidermis forming characteristic crater-like cankers.
diseases.cause: Fungus entering through fruit abrasions, insect punctures, and hail wounds.
organic_treatment: Spray Copper Hydroxide @ 2 g/L
Neem seed kernel extract 5%
prevention: Protect fruits from mechanical wind abrasions by planting windbreaks
Control insect pests that puncture fruit rind

diseases.name: Tea Mosquito Bug (Helopeltis antonii)
diseases.symptoms: Reddish-brown necrotic spot punctures on tender shoots and fruit rind; fruits become scabby, deformed, hard, and stunted with black corky spots.
diseases.cause: Mirid bug nymph and adult sucking sap from young shoots and developing fruitlets.
organic_treatment: Spray 3% neem oil with soap
Conserve predatory spiders and reduviid bugs
prevention: Prune canopy to avoid damp dense microclimates
Spray at flushing and fruitlet setting stages

name: Neem
how_to_identify_leaf: Imparipinnate compound leaves (20-40 cm) with 20-30 distinctly asymmetric, curved, sickle-shaped lanceolate leaflets with sharply serrated (toothed) margins and bitter taste.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Smooth oval or ellipsoid drupe (1.5-2.0 cm), green turning bright greenish-yellow when ripe; thin sweetish pulp enclosing a white hard bony shell with an oily kernel.
lookalikes: Mahanimb / Bakayan (Melia azedarach - bipinnate leaves, round drupes, toxic seeds)
season: Flowering in March-May; Fruit maturity in June-August during monsoon
soil: Thrives on dry, stony, shallow, alkaline soils; deep taproot system; cannot tolerate freezing temperatures or waterlogged soils
water: Highly drought-hardy; survives on 150-500 mm annual rainfall; virtually no supplemental irrigation needed once established
seed_rate_and_sowing: Propagated via fresh seeds (viability lost within 2-3 weeks); sow in nursery in July; Spacing: 8x8 m or 10x10 m for plantation/agroforestry
benefits: Unrivaled natural botanical pesticide and insect repellent (azadirachtin)
Potent antifungal, antibacterial, and antiviral properties across agriculture and health
Neem cake enriches soil nitrogen retention by inhibiting nitrification
risks_or_cautions: Neem seed oil is toxic for internal consumption in infants and children (can cause Reye-like syndrome)
Excessive internal consumption can impair fertility
medicinal_uses: Leaf paste used across Ayurveda for dermatological ailments (eczema, ringworm, acne, psoriasis)
Fresh tender twigs used traditionally as antibacterial datun toothbrushes

diseases.name: Tea Mosquito Bug / Blight (Helopeltis antonii)
diseases.symptoms: Black sunken necrotic spots on young tender shoots and leaves; shoot tip blight with drying and dieback of young flush.
diseases.cause: Mirid bug sucking sap from tender growing tips during post-monsoon flush.
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of 5% NSKE (ironically, neem extract repels its own pests!)
Spray Beauveria bassiana @ 5 g/L
prevention: Prune and remove severely affected shoots before spring

diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Oidium azadirachtae)
diseases.symptoms: White talcum-like powdery patches on upper leaf surfaces and young shoots causing leaf distortion, yellowing, and premature leaf drop.
diseases.cause: Ectophytic fungus thriving in cool dry weather with high morning humidity in Dec-Feb.
organic_treatment: Spray Wettable Sulfur 80% WDG @ 3 g/L
Foliar spray of cow urine (10%)
prevention: Prune dense branches to allow light penetration into tree center

diseases.name: Neem Scale / White Scale (Aonidiella orientalis / Parlatoria crypta)
diseases.symptoms: Crusts of tiny circular yellow or white waxy scale insects on stems, petioles and leaves; leaves turn yellow and drop; dieback of branches.
diseases.cause: Diaspidid scale insect sucking sap under protective waxy armour.
organic_treatment: Prune heavily encrusted twigs
Spray 2% horticultural mineral oil with soap to suffocate scales
Conserve Chilocorus nigrita predatory ladybird beetles
prevention: Avoid planting neem in overcrowded monocultures in low-sunlight locations

diseases.name: Leaf Spot / Anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides / Pseudocercospora)
diseases.symptoms: Circular to irregular dark brown spots with darker margins on leaflets; coalescing into extensive necrotic blighted areas during monsoon.
diseases.cause: Fungal pathogen active during heavy monsoon cloud cover and constant leaf wetness.
organic_treatment: Spray Bordeaux mixture 1%
Copper Oxychloride @ 3 g/L
prevention: Ensure wide spacing between trees
Collect and burn fallen diseased leaves

diseases.name: Damping Off in Nursery (Rhizoctonia solani / Pythium)
diseases.symptoms: Seedling collar rot at soil line causing newly emerged seedlings to topple and rot rapidly in nursery polybags.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne fungi favored by overwatering and dense nursery shading.
organic_treatment: Trichoderma harzianum @ 10 g/kg potting soil mix
Drench with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L
prevention: Use sand-rich porous potting mix
Avoid excess shade and overwatering in seedling beds

name: Tulsi
how_to_identify_leaf: Simple, opposite decussate ovate leaves (2-5 cm) with serrated margins, acute apex, covered with fine glandular hairs that exude a powerful sweet clove-like spicy aroma when rubbed.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Terminal spicate racemes with whorls of tiny purplish-pink or white bilabiate flowers; four tiny smooth nutlet seeds enclosed in persistent papery calyx.
lookalikes: Sweet Basil (Ocimum basilicum - larger, smoother leaves, anise aroma)
season: Planted year-round; thrives in warm tropical summer and monsoon; sensitive to extreme winter frost
soil: Fertile, well-drained loamy soil with good organic content; pH 6.0-7.5; water stagnation causes root rot within days
water: Moderate moisture; water when top inch of soil is dry; avoid wetting foliage in evening
seed_rate_and_sowing: Direct sowing: 1 kg/ha; Nursery transplanting: 250-300 g/ha; Spacing: 45x45 cm; Seeds are tiny, sow at 0.5 cm depth
benefits: Premier adaptogen supporting balanced cortisol response and psychological stress resilience
Eugenol provides powerful antimicrobial and bronchodilator activity
Enhances cellular immune defense
risks_or_cautions: May lower blood sugar and thin blood; exercise caution before scheduled surgeries or with anti-coagulant medications
Excessive intake of concentrated oil not recommended in pregnancy
medicinal_uses: Fresh leaf decoction with black pepper and ginger taken for viral fever, bronchitis, and upper respiratory catarrh
Crushed leaves applied topically to calm insect stings and ringworm

diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Oidium spp.)
diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth spreading over both leaf surfaces; leaves turn chlorotic, curl, and wither prematurely.
diseases.cause: Airborne fungus favored by moderate temperatures (20-25°C) and shade with high humidity.
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) 5 g/L with few drops of liquid soap
Spray diluted milk (1 part milk : 9 parts water) in morning sun
Wettable sulfur @ 2 g/L
chemical_treatment_type: Avoid synthetic systemic chemicals on medicinal tulsi; use Azoxystrobin @ 0.5 ml/L only if non-consumable crop
prevention: Place plants in full sun (at least 6 hours daily)
Avoid overhead watering; water at base only

diseases.name: Root Rot / Collar Rot (Rhizoctonia solani / Pythium)
diseases.symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of whole plant; stem base at soil line turns dark brown, soft and water-soaked; root system completely decays.
diseases.cause: Excess watering and poorly drained potting soil/beds during monsoon.
organic_treatment: Drench root zone with Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L
Incorporate neem cake into soil
Withhold irrigation until soil dries
prevention: Use sand and perlite mixed potting soil with drainage holes
Never allow water to stand in saucers

diseases.name: Aphids / Tulsi Lace Bug (Monanthia globulifera)
diseases.symptoms: Tiny black and white lace-winged bugs on leaf undersides; leaves develop fine white stipples, turn yellow, and dry; black tar-like frass on leaf backs.
diseases.cause: Tingid bug sucking sap from leaf undersides in warm weather.
organic_treatment: Spray cold water jet on undersides of leaves
Spray 2% neem oil mixed with organic soap
Spray garlic-chilli extract solution
chemical_treatment_type: Avoid toxic chemical sprays on home tulsi; use potassium salts of fatty acids (insecticidal soap)
prevention: Prune overcrowded shoots regularly to promote air flow
Encourage ladybird beetles

diseases.name: Leaf Spot (Cercospora ocimicola / Alternaria)
diseases.symptoms: Small, dark brown to black circular necrotic spots on leaves with pale yellow halos; leaves turn yellow and drop off.
diseases.cause: Fungal spores spread by rain splashes and overhead watering.
organic_treatment: Spray sour buttermilk solution (5%)
Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L
Bordeaux mixture 0.5%
prevention: Pluck and destroy spotted leaves immediately
Water early in morning so leaves dry quickly in sun

diseases.name: Iron Deficiency (Nutrient)
diseases.symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on youngest leaves; veins remain sharply dark green while leaf tissue between veins turns creamy yellow or white.
diseases.cause: Alkaline soil/water (pH > 7.5) rendering iron insoluble; overwatering causing root hypoxia.
organic_treatment: Apply composted vermicompost enriched with iron sulfate
Mulch with acidic pine needles or peat
chemical_treatment_type: Foliar spray of Chelated Iron (Fe-EDTA 12%) @ 1.0 g/L
prevention: Maintain potting soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8
Avoid hard water deposits in pots

name: Aloe vera
how_to_identify_leaf: Thick, fleshy, succulent lanceolate rosettes (30-50 cm long, 5-8 cm wide) with sharp pale triangular teeth on margins; smooth glaucous grayish-green skin; interior filled with clear viscous gelatinous mucilage.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Hanging tubular yellow or orange-red flowers produced on tall upright terminal scapes (up to 90 cm); triangular capsules with winged seeds; rarely sets viable seed under cultivation.
lookalikes: Agave americana (century plant - fibrous, toxic sap, huge sharp end spine)
season: Planted year-round; best established during monsoon (July-August)
soil: Extremely well-drained sandy or gravelly loam; cannot tolerate any standing water; thrives in pH 6.5-8.0; highly drought and salt tolerant
water: Very low water requirement; water only when soil is completely bone dry; overwatering is the #1 cause of plant death
seed_rate_and_sowing: Propagated exclusively by vegetative root suckers (pups); Population: 25,000 suckers/ha; Spacing: 60x60 cm or 60x45 cm
benefits: Acemannan accelerates cutaneous wound healing, collagen synthesis and thermal burn recovery
Topical anti-inflammatory, soothing and moisturizing agent for skin and hair
Supports gastrointestinal mucosal integrity
risks_or_cautions: Yellow latex directly beneath the rind contains aloin (anthraquinone) which is a harsh cathartic laxative causing abdominal cramps; discard yellow latex before consuming clear gel
Avoid ingestion during pregnancy
medicinal_uses: Fresh inner clear gel applied directly to minor sunburns, thermal burns, cuts, and irritated skin
Processed clear gel taken orally in traditional medicine to soothe peptic ulcers and acid reflux

diseases.name: Basal Stem and Root Rot (Pythium ultimum / Phytophthora nicotianae)
diseases.symptoms: Leaf bases near soil line turn soft, water-soaked, black and mushy; outer leaves collapse and detach easily; foul odor.
diseases.cause: Overwatering and poorly drained clay soils; fungi thrive in wet, poorly aerated root environments.
organic_treatment: Withhold water completely; unpot, trim off black rotten roots, dust with cinnamon powder/charcoal, air-dry for 3 days and repot in dry sandy soil
Trichoderma viride drench
chemical_treatment_type: Drenching with Metalaxyl 35% WS @ 2 g/L or Copper Oxychloride @ 3 g/L
prevention: Use porous succulent potting mix (50% coarse sand/perlite, 50% soil)
Never let water pool in central leaf rosette

diseases.name: Aloe Rust (Uromyces aloes)
diseases.symptoms: Small, raised, round, dark brown to black circular lesions surrounded by yellow halos on both leaf surfaces; lesions harden into black corky spots.
diseases.cause: Obligate fungal pathogen favoured by cool damp air and overhead irrigation.
organic_treatment: Prune and destroy severely spotted outer leaves
Spray 3% neem oil or wettable sulfur @ 2 g/L
prevention: Water at soil level without splashing leaves
Place in full bright sun with good ventilation

diseases.name: Anthracnose / Leaf Spot (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides)
diseases.symptoms: Round, sunken, dark brown to black spots on leaves; spots dry out, crack, and turn leathery; ruins aesthetic and gel quality.
diseases.cause: Fungal spores spread by rain and overhead water in warm humid conditions.
organic_treatment: Spray Bordeaux mixture 1%
Pseudomonas fluorescens foliar spray @ 5 g/L
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation
Ensure wide spacing (60 cm) between plants

diseases.name: Aloe Mite / Gall Mite (Aceria aloinis)
diseases.symptoms: Bizarre, grotesque, cauliflower-like tumorous warty outgrowths (galls) on flower stems and leaves ('aloe cancer'); stunting of plant.
diseases.cause: Microscopic eriophyid mite injecting toxins while feeding.
organic_treatment: Cut off the entire gall tissue with a sterile knife and destroy by burning; treat wound with sulfur paste
Isolate infested plants immediately
prevention: Never propagate from mite-infested parent plants; quarantine new accessions

diseases.name: Mealybugs (Pseudococcus spp.)
diseases.symptoms: White cottony waxy clusters deep in the leaf axils and crevices between leaves; leaves turn yellow, weaken, and develop sooty mold.
diseases.cause: Sap-sucking insects thriving in dry sheltered leaf bases.
organic_treatment: Dab individual clusters with cotton swab dipped in 70% isopropyl alcohol
Spray 2% neem oil mixed with soap spray directed deep into leaf axils
chemical_treatment_type: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 ml/L drench around root zone
prevention: Inspect crevices of new suckers before transplanting

name: Turmeric
how_to_identify_leaf: Large, oblong-lanceolate smooth leaves (70-100 cm long, 15-20 cm wide) emerging directly from underground rhizome on long petioles; prominent parallel veins; aromatic ginger-like scent when bruised.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Fleshy branched underground tuberous rhizome ('fingers' and 'mother bulbs'); rough brownish skin, bright golden-orange internal flesh; flowers produced on central spike with greenish-pink bracts; rarely sets seed.
season: Planted in May-June (Kharif); harvested in Jan-March (8-9 month crop duration)
soil: Well-drained rich loamy or alluvial soil high in organic matter; pH 5.5-7.5; highly sensitive to waterlogging which causes rhizome rot
water: 1500-2000 mm; requires 15-20 irrigations in plains; critical during rhizome development stage; withhold water 15-20 days before harvest
seed_rate_and_sowing: Whole or split healthy rhizome fingers (20-30g): 2000-2500 kg/ha; Planted on ridges or raised beds; Spacing: 30x20 cm; Depth: 4-5 cm; Mulching immediately with green leaves (15 t/ha) is mandatory
benefits: Curcumin provides clinically demonstrated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and hepatoprotective properties
Extremely dense dietary source of iron and trace minerals
Natural food preservative and golden colorant
risks_or_cautions: High intake of curcumin supplements contraindicated for individuals with gallstones or bile duct obstruction
May enhance effects of blood thinners
medicinal_uses: Turmeric milk (Haldi doodh) consumed traditionally across India for acute inflammation, wounds, and colds
Topical antiseptic paste applied to cuts, burns, and post-partum healing

diseases.name: Rhizome Rot / Soft Rot (Pythium aphanidermatum)
diseases.symptoms: Collar region becomes water-soaked and soft; lower leaves yellow and dry from margins inward; pseudostem easily pulls out from rhizome; rhizome rots into foul-smelling brown mush.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne oomycete favored by waterlogging, heavy soils, and continuous rainy spells (28-30°C).
organic_treatment: Rhizome seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 10 g/kg
Soil application of Trichoderma enriched neem cake (2 tonnes/ha)
Drench with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L
chemical_treatment_type: Rhizome dip and soil drench with Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L
prevention: Always plant on raised beds (15-20 cm high) with deep drainage channels
Select disease-free seed rhizomes from healthy plots
Crop rotation with non-hosts like maize or paddy

diseases.name: Leaf Blotch (Taphrina maculans)
diseases.symptoms: Numerous small, circular or oval yellow-brown spots (1-2 mm) appearing in clusters on upper leaf surface, coalescing into large dirty-yellow patches.
diseases.cause: Airborne fungal ascospores active in cool humid conditions (20-25°C).
organic_treatment: Spray Bordeaux mixture 1%
Foliar spray of 5% NSKE
prevention: Collect and burn diseased foliage after harvest
Avoid dense shade in intercropped orchards

diseases.name: Leaf Spot (Colletotrichum capsici)
diseases.symptoms: Large, elliptical or oblong brown spots with greyish-white centers and dark brown margins; central area develops concentric rings of black dots (acervuli).
diseases.cause: Fungus favored by warm, rainy, overcast weather in August-September.
organic_treatment: Spray Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L
Spray fresh cow urine solution (10%)
prevention: Spray at first onset of spots during monsoon
Follow crop rotation

diseases.name: Shoot Borer (Conogethes punctiferalis)
diseases.symptoms: Central shoots turn yellow and dry up ('dead heart'); bore holes plugged with dark extruded frass visible on the pseudostem.
diseases.cause: Crambid moth caterpillar boring into pseudostem to feed on internal vascular core.
organic_treatment: Prune and destroy bored pseudostems containing larvae
Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 2 g/L
Spray 3% neem oil @ 3 ml/L
prevention: Monitor for adult moths in August-October
Light traps to attract adult moths

diseases.name: Turmeric Thrips (Panchaetothrips indicus)
diseases.symptoms: Leaves roll up from margins; yellowing and gradual drying of leaf tips; silvery streaks on leaf surface.
diseases.cause: Thrips active during dry spells following monsoon.
organic_treatment: Spray neem oil 1500 ppm @ 3 ml/L with soap
Blue sticky traps @ 20/ha
prevention: Maintain optimum soil moisture; avoid water stress during dry spells

name: Ginger
how_to_identify_leaf: Slender, reed-like pseudostem bearing alternate, narrow, linear-lanceolate smooth leaves (15-20 cm long, 2 cm wide) with sheathing bases; spicy pungent aromatic fragrance when crushed.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Knobby, palmate, fibrous subterranean branched rhizome ('hands'); beige to pale yellowish-brown corky skin; pale yellow pungent spicy interior flesh; sterile triploid, produces no seeds.
lookalikes: Turmeric (Curcuma longa - much broader paddle leaves)
season: Planted in April-May (pre-monsoon); harvested in Dec-Feb (8-9 months after planting)
soil: Rich, loose, well-aerated sandy loam, clay loam or laterite soil rich in humus; pH 5.5-6.5; extremely sensitive to poor drainage
water: 1500-2000 mm; requires steady moisture; 4-6 leaf mulches applied during growth to retain moisture; withhold water 1 month before harvest
seed_rate_and_sowing: Carefully selected disease-free seed rhizome pieces (20-25g with at least 1-2 good buds): 1500-1800 kg/ha; Raised beds (15 cm high, 1 m wide); Spacing: 25x20 cm; Depth: 4-5 cm
benefits: Gingerol compounds exert clinically proven anti-emetic actions for nausea, motion sickness and pregnancy sickness
Strong anti-inflammatory activity alleviates muscle soreness and osteoarthritic discomfort
Promotes gastric emptying and reduces dyspepsia
risks_or_cautions: High doses may cause mild heartburn or diarrhea in sensitive stomachs
Mild anti-platelet aggregation; consult physician if on blood thinners
medicinal_uses: Fresh ginger juice with honey used traditionally for coughs, sore throat, and digestive sluggishness
Dry ginger powder (Sunthi) used in Ayurveda for joint stiffness and indigestion

diseases.name: Soft Rot / Rhizome Rot (Pythium aphanidermatum / P. myriotylum)
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on pseudostem collar; leaves yellow rapidly from base upward; pseudostem easily slips out of the rhizome; rhizome rots into foul-smelling soft watery decay.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne oomycete pathogen exploding in waterlogged, poorly drained beds during heavy monsoon.
organic_treatment: Rhizome seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum @ 10 g/kg
Soil application of Trichoderma enriched neem cake (2.5 t/ha)
Drenching with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L
chemical_treatment_type: Seed rhizome dip and drench with Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L
prevention: Mandatory planting on raised beds (15 cm high)
Never plant in water-stagnant plots
Strict selection of rot-free seed rhizomes; 3-year crop rotation

diseases.name: Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum)
diseases.symptoms: Lower leaves curl and droop; bronze-green wilting followed by rapid yellowing; vascular rings in rhizome turn dark brown; milky white bacterial ooze flows when cut stem is dipped in clean water.
diseases.cause: Bacterium surviving in soil and infected seed rhizomes; spreads through irrigation water.
organic_treatment: Soil solarization of beds for 30 days in summer
Drench with fresh cow dung extract + Pseudomonas
Apply bleaching powder @ 15 kg/ha before planting
chemical_treatment_type: Drenching with Streptocycline 1g + Copper Oxychloride 25g in 10L water
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed rhizomes
Maintain dedicated isolation channels between beds to stop runoff

diseases.name: Shoot Borer (Conogethes punctiferalis)
diseases.symptoms: Yellowing and drying of central shoot ('dead heart'); bore hole with frass visible on pseudostem.
diseases.cause: Larva boring into pseudostem.
organic_treatment: Prune and destroy bored pseudostems
Spray Bacillus thuringiensis @ 2 g/L
Spray 3% neem oil
prevention: Pheromone traps in September-October
Destroy wild host plants around borders

diseases.name: Leaf Spot / Phyllosticta Blight (Phyllosticta zingiberi)
diseases.symptoms: Small, oval to elongated yellowish spots with white papery centers and dark brown margins; centers often tear into shot holes.
diseases.cause: Fungus spreading during continuous rainy spells in July-August.
organic_treatment: Spray Bordeaux mixture 1%
Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L
prevention: Apply heavy leaf mulch (green leaf mulching) to protect foliage from soil splash
Spray before heavy monsoon sets in

diseases.name: Root Knot Nematode (Meloidogyne incognita)
diseases.symptoms: Galls and swellings on roots; brown water-soaked lesions on rhizome surface; leaves turn pale yellow; plants are stunted and unthrifty.
diseases.cause: Microscopic endoparasitic roundworm creating entry wounds for soft rot and bacterial wilt.
organic_treatment: Apply Paecilomyces lilacinus (nematode-egg parasitic fungus) @ 10 g/m² in beds
Apply neem cake @ 1 t/ha in soil
chemical_treatment_type: Fluensulfone 2% G @ 10 kg/ha or Carbofuran 3% G in planting furrows
prevention: Intercrop with marigold (Tagetes erecta)
Hot water treatment of seed rhizomes at 48°C for 20 minutes

name: Mustard
how_to_identify_leaf: Lyrate-pinnatifid lower leaves with large terminal lobe and smaller lateral lobes; upper leaves lanceolate, sessile, entire; bright green with pungent wasabi-like glucosinolate taste.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Slender, cylindrical, two-valved pods (siliqua) 3-5 cm long with a prominent conical beak; containing 10-20 tiny, spherical, smooth, reddish-brown to black pungent seeds.
lookalikes: Rapeseed / Toria (Brassica campestris - leaves clasp the stem)
season: Rabi (sown Sept-Oct; harvested Feb-March)
soil: Light to heavy loams with good drainage; pH 6.0-7.5; thrives on conserved winter moisture in northern alluvial plains
water: 200-300 mm; 2-3 irrigations (Pre-sowing, flowering, and pod filling stages); highly drought-tolerant compared to wheat
seed_rate_and_sowing: 4-5 kg/ha; Spacing: 30x10 cm; Depth: 2-3 cm (sowing deeper than 3 cm severely impedes germination)
benefits: Major domestic edible oil source across North and Eastern India
High smoke point mustard oil ideal for traditional Indian cooking
Glucosinolates and isothiocyanates exhibit potent antimicrobial action
risks_or_cautions: Raw cold-pressed high-erucic acid mustard oil requires moderation
Can cause skin blistering if applied neat under occlusion
medicinal_uses: Warm mustard oil massage traditionally used for chest congestion, arthritic joints, and muscular soreness
Warm mustard seed foot baths used for relieving winter chills

diseases.name: Mustard Aphid (Lipaphis erysimi)
diseases.symptoms: Devastating clusters of greenish-white tiny lice smothering inflorescence, buds, and pods; plants turn pale, wilt, and set zero seeds; sticky honeydew causes black sooty mold.
diseases.cause: Homopteran pest multiplying exponentially in cloudy, cold, humid weather (15-20°C) during Jan-Feb.
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of 5% NSKE at first sight of aphid colonies
Spray 3% neem oil or insecticidal soap solution
Conserve Coccinella septempunctata ladybird beetles
prevention: Timely early sowing (before October 15) escapes peak aphid population
Avoid excessive nitrogen application

diseases.name: White Rust (Albugo candida)
diseases.symptoms: Prominent, shiny, white or creamy blister-like pustules on leaf undersides; hypertrophy and staghead malformation of floral parts causing complete sterility.
diseases.cause: Oomycete favored by moist cool conditions (10-18°C) with heavy morning dew.
organic_treatment: Spray Bordeaux mixture 1%
Seed treatment with Trichoderma @ 10 g/kg
prevention: Use resistant varieties like Pusa Mustard 25, RH-406
Destroy infected staghead panicles
Clean seedbed
