diseases.name: Alternaria Leaf Blight (Alternaria brassicae)
diseases.symptoms: Small brown to black spots with concentric rings on leaves, stems and pods; spots coalesce, pods turn brittle and shatter prematurely; shriveled seeds.
diseases.cause: Air and seed-borne fungus active in damp weather with intermittent rains (15-25°C).
organic_treatment: Spray 10% cow urine extract
Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L
prevention: Seed treatment with Captan or Thiram @ 3 g/kg
Burn crop residue after harvest

diseases.name: Downy Mildew (Hyaloperonospora parasitica)
diseases.symptoms: Yellowish angular patches on upper leaf surface with white to grayish downy fungal growth on corresponding undersides; often occurs together with white rust.
diseases.cause: Oomycete pathogen exploding in cold foggy mornings.
organic_treatment: Spray Copper Hydroxide @ 2 g/L
Spray fresh buttermilk extract (50 ml/L)
prevention: Seed treatment with Metalaxyl 35% WS @ 4 g/kg
Wider row spacing to reduce humidity in canopy

diseases.name: Sclerotinia Stem Rot (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum)
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on main stem near soil line turning bleached chalky-white; stem splits open revealing large, hard, black rat-dropping-like sclerotia inside.
diseases.cause: Soil-borne fungus surviving as sclerotia in soil for 5+ years; favoured by high plant density and heavy canopy.
organic_treatment: Deep summer ploughing to bury sclerotia
Soil application of Coniothyrium minitans or Trichoderma @ 5 kg/ha
prevention: Avoid excessive flood irrigation
Crop rotation with non-host crops like wheat, barley, or gram
Avoid dense plant populations

name: Groundnut
how_to_identify_leaf: Evenly pinnate compound leaves with 4 oval to obovate leaflets arranged in two opposite pairs; leaflets fold together at night (nyctinastic movements).
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Underground indehiscent reticulated cylindrical pod (peg burrows into soil after pollination) containing 1-4 oval seeds with reddish-brown or pink papery seed coat and two large oily cotyledons.
season: Kharif (sown June-July; 80% area), Rabi / Summer (sown Nov-Dec or Jan-Feb under irrigation)
soil: Well-drained loose, friable sandy loam or red sandy loam rich in calcium; pH 6.0-7.0; heavy clay severely hinders peg penetration and causes pod breakage during harvest
water: 450-650 mm; critical stages: Flowering, Pegging (30-45 DAS), and Pod formation (50-70 DAS); avoid water stress at pegging
seed_rate_and_sowing: Bunch varieties: 100-110 kg kernels/ha; Spreading varieties: 90-100 kg kernels/ha; Spacing: 30x10 cm; Depth: 4-5 cm in moist soil
benefits: Exceptionally protein-dense plant food; fundamental in rural diets and malnutrition recovery (RUTF)
Heart-healthy mono- and polyunsaturated fatty acids
Resveratrol and phytosterols support vascular health
risks_or_cautions: Common severe food allergen capable of triggering life-threatening anaphylaxis
Improper drying and storage invites Aspergillus flavus producing carcinogenic aflatoxins
medicinal_uses: Groundnut oil (arachis oil) used as pharmaceutical vehicle for oil-based injections and therapeutic skin emollients
Peanut paste utilized in enriched therapeutic feeding protocols

diseases.name: Tikka Disease / Early & Late Leaf Spot (Cercospora arachidicola & Phaeoisariopsis personata)
diseases.symptoms: Early spot: circular reddish-brown spots with prominent bright yellow halos; Late spot: smaller, darker, carbon-black circular spots without prominent halos; heavy defoliation.
diseases.cause: Air and seed-borne fungi rampant during warm rainy spells (25-30°C and >80% RH).
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of 5% neem seed kernel extract (NSKE)
Spray fermented butter-milk (50 ml/L) mixed with copper oxychloride
prevention: Intercrop with pearl millet or pigeon pea (6:1 ratio)
Use resistant varieties like Kadiri-6, TAG-24, GPBD-4
Seed treatment with Carbendazim 2g/kg

diseases.name: Groundnut Rust (Puccinia arachidis)
diseases.symptoms: Small, orange-brown pustules on leaf undersides, rupturing to release powdery urediniospores; leaves curl, dry up, and remain attached without falling.
diseases.cause: Airborne spores blown by monsoon winds, often appearing alongside late leaf spot.
organic_treatment: Spray 3% neem oil @ 3 ml/L
Spray Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L
prevention: Combined spray for leaf spot and rust with Tebuconazole + Trifloxystrobin
Destroy volunteer groundnut plants

diseases.name: Collar Rot / Crown Rot (Aspergillus niger)
diseases.symptoms: Collar region rots at soil line covered with black sooty fungal powder; seedlings topple over; mature plants wilt rapidly.
diseases.cause: Seed and soil-borne fungus active in high soil temperatures and drought stress at germination.
organic_treatment: Seed bio-priming with Trichoderma viride @ 10 g/kg
Soil application of neem cake @ 250 kg/ha
chemical_treatment_type: Seed treatment with Thiram 37.5% + Carboxin 37.5% WS @ 2 g/kg seed
prevention: Deep summer ploughing
Avoid planting damaged, cracked or shriveled seed kernels

diseases.name: White Grub (Holotrichia consanguinea)
diseases.symptoms: C-shaped white grubs chew off tap roots and developing root pods; plants wilt and dry up in patches across the field.
diseases.cause: Scarabaeid beetle larva active in sandy soils during monsoon rains (July-August).
organic_treatment: Install light traps at first monsoon rain to catch adult beetles on neem and ber trees
Soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae @ 5 kg/ha with FYM
chemical_treatment_type: Seed treatment with Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 25 ml/kg or Imidacloprid 600 FS @ 6.5 ml/kg seed
Soil application of Fipronil 0.3% G @ 20 kg/ha
prevention: Deep summer ploughing exposes grubs to birds
Spray surrounding host trees (neem, ber, acacia) with monocrotophos at first monsoon shower

diseases.name: Spodoptera / Tobacco Caterpillar (Spodoptera litura)
diseases.symptoms: Gregarious young larvae skeletonize leaves into papery white webs; older solitary caterpillars voraciously defoliate canopy overnight.
diseases.cause: Polyphagous noctuid moth active during warm humid monsoon weather.
organic_treatment: Hand-pick and destroy egg masses and skeletonized leaves with young clusters
Install pheromone traps with Spodolure @ 10/ha
Spray SlNPV @ 250 LE/ha with 0.5% jaggery
prevention: Grow castor (Ricinus communis) as border/trap crop around the groundnut field
Collect larvae under soil clods during daytime

name: Cotton
how_to_identify_leaf: Large, alternate, palmately 3-5 lobed leaves with cordate base, prominent nectary glands on underside of main veins, and stipules at petiole base.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Ovoid, 3-5 locular leathery capsule ('boll') with smooth green rind with oil glands; splits open at maturity into 3-5 locks revealing fluffy white lint fibers adhering to dark brown fuzzy seeds.
season: Kharif (sown April-May in North India, June-July in Central & South India; 150-180 day crop)
soil: Deep, fertile Black Cotton Soils (Vertisols) with high clay content and moisture retention; pH 7.0-8.5; can also grow on deep alluvial soils with irrigation
water: 700-1200 mm; critical stages: Square formation, Flowering, and Boll development; water stress at flowering causes severe square/boll drop
seed_rate_and_sowing: Bt Hybrid cotton: 2.0-2.5 kg/ha (with 120g non-Bt refuge); Spacing: 90x60 cm or 120x60 cm; Depth: 4-5 cm in ridges and furrows
benefits: World's most important natural textile fiber ('White Gold')
Cottonseed oil is an important domestic edible oil after refining
Cottonseed cake is an invaluable protein-rich cattle feed
risks_or_cautions: Raw unrefined cottonseed contains toxic gossypol pigment causing heart and liver damage; safe only after commercial refining or for ruminants with bacterial detox
medicinal_uses: Cotton root bark decoction used historically in folk medicine as uterine stimulant (oxytocic)
Sterile cotton lint is the universal medical standard for surgical dressing and absorbent swabs

diseases.name: Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella)
diseases.symptoms: Rosetted flowers that fail to open properly; bore holes sealed with silk; larvae burrow inside developing green bolls feeding directly on seeds, staining lint pinkish-brown and ruining fiber.
diseases.cause: Gelechiid moth whose pink larva developed resistance to Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab Bt proteins in Central and Western India.
organic_treatment: Install Gossyplure pheromone traps @ 10 traps/ha for monitoring and 25/ha for mass trapping
Trichogrammatoidea bactrae egg parasitoid release @ 150,000/ha
Neem oil 1500 ppm @ 3 ml/L
prevention: Strictly terminate the crop by December-January; do not allow ratoon cotton
Deep summer ploughing to destroy overwintering diapausing larvae in double seeds
Comply with non-Bt refuge sowing requirements

diseases.name: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV)
diseases.symptoms: Upward or downward leaf curling with thick swollen veins; leafy enations (outgrowths) on underside of main veins; severe stunting of plant with minimal boll formation.
diseases.cause: Begomovirus complex with DNA-beta satellite transmitted exclusively by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci); rampant in North Indian cotton belt.
organic_treatment: Install yellow sticky traps @ 25/ha
Spray 5% NSKE or Neem oil (10,000 ppm) @ 2 ml/L
Rogue out early infected plants
prevention: Sow CLCuV-tolerant certified hybrids
Complete sowing before May 15 in North zone
Eradicate alternate weed hosts like Abutilon indicum and Xanthium strumarium

diseases.name: Bacterial Blight / Black Arm (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum)
diseases.symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots bounded by leaf veinlets (angular leaf spot); black lesions on petioles and stems causing snapping (black arm); circular water-soaked sunken spots on bolls (boll rot).
diseases.cause: Seed and debris-borne bacterium spreading via driving rain splashes and irrigation water.
organic_treatment: Seed acid delinting with concentrated sulfuric acid (100 ml/kg seed) to destroy seed-borne inoculum
Spray fresh cow dung extract @ 20 g/L
chemical_treatment_type: Streptocycline 1g + Copper Oxychloride 25g in 10L water foliar spray
prevention: Use acid-delinted certified seeds only
Avoid sprinkler overhead irrigation
Burn harvested cotton stalks

diseases.name: Cotton Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
diseases.symptoms: Tiny white moth-like flies flutter when canopy is disturbed; nymph clusters on leaf undersides suck sap causing leaf yellowing and shedding; sticky honeydew produces heavy black sooty mold; vectors CLCuD.
diseases.cause: Aleyrodid pest favored by hot, humid weather and dry spells in July-September.
organic_treatment: Yellow sticky traps @ 30/ha
Foliar spray of neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%)
Verticillium lecanii spray @ 5 g/L
prevention: Avoid excessive application of nitrogen fertilizers
Avoid early prophylactic synthetic pyrethroid sprays which cause whitefly flare-up

diseases.name: Grey Mildew / Dahiya Disease (Ramularia areola)
diseases.symptoms: Angular, pale translucent spots bounded by veinlets covered with frosty-white powdery mildew-like growth on leaf undersides; severe premature defoliation.
diseases.cause: Fungus active in late season under cool, humid conditions (20-25°C) with morning dew.
organic_treatment: Spray wettable sulfur 80% WDG @ 3 g/L
Spray fermented buttermilk (5%)
prevention: Wider spacing to promote canopy aeration
Prophylactic sulfur spray in October-November

name: Sugarcane
how_to_identify_leaf: Long, narrow, sword-like linear leaves (1-1.5 m long, 4-7 cm wide) with sharp, finely serrated razor-like margins, prominent white fibrous midrib, and overlapping sheaths clasping the solid stem.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Tall, thick, jointed solid cylindrical stalk (2-4 m high, 2-5 cm diameter) with distinct nodes and internodes; skin green, yellow, purple, or striped with white waxy bloom; sweet fibrous sucrose-rich pith; produces large feathery silver plume inflorescence ('arrow').
season: Autumn planting (Oct-Nov), Spring planting (Feb-March), Adsali planting in Maharashtra (July-Aug, 18-month crop)
soil: Deep, well-drained, fertile loams or clayey loams with high water retention and organic content; pH 6.5-7.5; water table below 1.5m
water: 1500-2500 mm; high water requirement; requires 20-30 irrigations in tropical zone; critical during formative tillering and grand growth stages; drip saves 40% water
seed_rate_and_sowing: Three-budded healthy setts: 40,000-45,000 setts/ha (approx. 6-8 tonnes/ha); Furrow planting at 90 cm or 120 cm (paired row 150 cm); Depth: 7-10 cm
benefits: Source of 80% of world's sugar and domestic jaggery (gur)
Byproducts provide ethanol biofuel (molasses), paper & green power cogeneration (bagasse), and organic fertilizer (pressmud)
Raw juice provides quick rehydration and glycogen replenishment
risks_or_cautions: High glycemic index concentrated sucrose requires restriction in diabetic diets
Unsanitary roadside juice extraction can harbor enteric foodborne pathogens
medicinal_uses: Fresh sugarcane juice consumed traditionally in Ayurveda to soothe jaundice and support liver recovery
Black strap molasses used as natural mineral-dense remedy for iron deficiency anemia

diseases.name: Red Rot (Colletotrichum falcatum)
diseases.symptoms: Third or fourth leaf from top shows yellowing and withering; longitudinal split of stalk shows blood-red internal pith with distinct white horizontal patches/bands across red tissue; sour alcoholic odor.
diseases.cause: Fungus entering through root primordia, node cracks, and borer holes; spread by diseased seed setts and flood irrigation.
organic_treatment: Hot water treatment of setts at 52°C for 30 minutes
Moist hot air treatment (MHAT) at 54°C for 2.5 hours
Trichoderma viride sett dip @ 10 g/L
chemical_treatment_type: Sett treatment: Dip setts in Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/L or Thiophanate Methyl 70% WP for 15 minutes before planting
prevention: Plant resistant varieties (e.g., Co-0238, Co-86032, CoM-0265)
Rogue out and burn infected clumps with roots immediately
Adopt crop rotation with paddy or green manure crops

diseases.name: Sugarcane Smut (Sporisorium scitamineum)
diseases.symptoms: Terminal growing point produces a long, black, whip-like, curved unbranched structure (up to 1 m long) covered with millions of black sooty teliospores; leaves become narrow, stiff and erect.
diseases.cause: Internally and externally seed and wind-borne fungal teliospores entering through bud scales.
organic_treatment: Carefully cover whip in a polythene bag, cut off and burn to prevent spore dispersal
Dip setts in Trichoderma slurry
chemical_treatment_type: Sett dip in Triadimefon 25% WP @ 1 g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L for 15 minutes
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed canes from healthy nurseries
Avoid taking ratoon crops from smut-infected fields
Plant resistant varieties

diseases.name: Early Shoot Borer (Chilo infuscatellus)
diseases.symptoms: Dead heart in young shoots (1-3 months old); dead shoot pulls out easily emitting a foul rotten odor; horizontal pin-holes at base of shoot.
diseases.cause: Crambid moth caterpillar boring into young shoot base in hot dry weather (March-June).
organic_treatment: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis @ 50,000/ha weekly from 30 to 90 days
Light earthing up of canes at 30-45 days to bury base
Trash mulching on furrows (3 t/ha) at 3 days after planting
chemical_treatment_type: Soil application of Fipronil 0.3% G @ 25 kg/ha or Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% G @ 18 kg/ha at planting in furrows
prevention: Plant early (February) to establish tillers before peak summer
Frequent light summer irrigations reduce shoot borer attack

diseases.name: Internode Borer (Chilo sacchariphagus indicus)
diseases.symptoms: Constricted internodes with entrance holes plugged with fresh frass; tissues inside turn red (often confused with red rot); reduction in cane length and juice sucrose.
diseases.cause: Borer attacking older canes from 4th month onward till harvest.
organic_treatment: Release Trichogramma chilonis @ 50,000/ha fortnightly from 4th month to harvest
Detrashing: strip and remove lower dry senescent leaves periodically
chemical_treatment_type: Foliar spray of Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3 ml/L directed into leaf sheaths
prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen application
Select clean non-bored seed canes

diseases.name: Grassy Shoot Disease (GSD)
diseases.symptoms: Proliferation of numerous thin, spindly, pale white or chlorotic tillers resembling a tuft of grass; complete absence of cane formation; severe stunting.
diseases.cause: Phytoplasma transmitted by cane leafhoppers and aphid vectors (Rhopalosiphum maidis); perpetuates through infected seed setts.
organic_treatment: Rogue and destroy diseased clumps immediately
Hot water treatment of setts at 50°C for 2 hours
prevention: Raise three-tier seed nursery system (breeder, foundation, certified)
Never use setts from ratoon fields showing GSD symptoms

name: Variegated Foliage
how_to_identify_leaf: Ovate to elliptic leaves featuring distinct cream-white or pale ivory margins surrounding an emerald green central lamina, smooth entire margins, and arcuate venation.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Ornamental cultivars rarely set fruit in indoor/garden culture; white pithy drupes or small syconium figs may form outdoors.
season: Year-round perennial ornamental foliage; best growth during warm monsoon and spring flushes
soil: Rich, well-draining loamy potting mix enriched with leaf mold and perlite; pH 6.0-7.0
water: Moderate watering; allow top 2 cm of soil to dry between irrigations; avoid waterlogging
seed_rate_and_sowing: Propagated via semi-hardwood stem cuttings or air layering during warm rainy season
benefits: Air-purifying ornamental landscape shrub
Striking bicolored foliage architecture
Excellent low-maintenance hedging and indoor pot plant
risks_or_cautions: Non-edible ornamental foliage; sap may cause mild skin sensitivity in sensitive individuals
medicinal_uses: Mainly cultivated for aesthetic biophilic design and urban air quality enhancement

diseases.name: Anthracnose & Leaf Margin Burn (Colletotrichum spp.)
diseases.symptoms: Browning and necrosis along the non-chlorophyll white margins, leading to dry ragged leaf edges and premature leaf drop.
diseases.cause: Overwatering, overhead wetting of leaves in low light, or stagnant humid air.
organic_treatment: Prune browned variegated foliage
Spray cold-pressed Neem Oil @ 3 ml/L
Improve air circulation
chemical_treatment_type: Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L
prevention: Avoid wetting foliage when watering
Provide bright filtered indirect sunlight to protect white margins from scorching

name: Citrus / Lemon
how_to_identify_leaf: Alternate, dark glossy green elliptical leaves with winged petioles and fine pellucid oil glands that emit a fresh citrus fragrance when crushed.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Globose to oval hesperidium fruit with yellow to green glandular peel (flavedo) containing acidic juicy pulp vesicles.
season: Year-round fruiting with main flushes in Hastabahar and Ambebahar
soil: Well-drained sandy loam to alluvial soils, pH 5.5-7.5; highly sensitive to waterlogging
water: Regular drip irrigation; stress period of 3-4 weeks given before flowering to induce profuse bloom
seed_rate_and_sowing: Budded or air-layered grafts planted at 5m x 5m or 6m x 6m spacing
benefits: Immune-boosting high Vitamin C source
Aids digestive absorption and kidney stone prevention
Versatile culinary acidulant
risks_or_cautions: High acidity can erode dental enamel if consumed undiluted
medicinal_uses: Ayurvedic Nimbu swarasa used in digestive formulations and detoxifying beverages

diseases.name: Citrus Canker (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri)
diseases.symptoms: Raised, corky, rough brownish lesions with characteristic yellow chlorotic halos on both leaf surfaces, twigs, and fruits.
diseases.cause: Bacterium entering through stomata or leaf-miner wounds, dispersed by wind-driven rain.
organic_treatment: Prune and burn cankered twigs before monsoon
Spray 1% Bordeaux mixture or Copper Hydroxide @ 2 g/L
chemical_treatment_type: Streptocycline 1g in 10L water mixed with Copper Oxychloride 30g
prevention: Control citrus leaf miner using Neem oil or spinosad
Erect windbreak trees around orchard

name: Rose
how_to_identify_leaf: Alternate odd-pinnately compound leaves with 3 to 7 oval, sharply serrated leaflets, dark green upper surface, and paired stipules at petiole base.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Showy multi-petaled fragrant flowers followed by fleshy berry-like red to orange rose hips.
season: Winter to spring peak bloom across plains; year-round in temperate highlands
soil: Fertile clay loam rich in organic manure; well-drained, pH 6.0-6.8
water: Deep regular watering at root base; avoid splashing water on flower buds and leaves
seed_rate_and_sowing: Propagated via T-budding or rooted hardwood cuttings
benefits: Premium commercial cut flower and essential oil extraction
Petals used for Gulkand and herbal tea
Natural mood uplifter
risks_or_cautions: Sharp epidermal prickles (thorns) require handling care
medicinal_uses: Gulab jal (Rose water) used as eye soothing wash and cosmetic toner
Gulkand treats hyperacidity

diseases.name: Black Spot (Diplocarpon rosae)
diseases.symptoms: Circular black spots with feathery fringed margins on upper leaf surfaces, surrounded by yellow chlorotic tissue, followed by rapid defoliation.
diseases.cause: Fungal spores germinating in leaf wetness lasting >6 hours in humid weather.
organic_treatment: Remove and dispose of fallen infected leaves
Baking soda spray (5g/L with 2 ml liquid soap)
Foliar neem oil spray @ 4 ml/L
chemical_treatment_type: Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 ml/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Azoxystrobin @ 1 ml/L
prevention: Prune inner branches for sun penetration
Water strictly at soil level early morning

name: Mint
how_to_identify_leaf: Opposite, aromatic, ovate to lanceolate bright green leaves with serrated margins, prominent veins, square stems, and strong menthol aroma.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Tiny purple to lilac flower spikes in whorled verticillasters; small nutlets.
season: Spring, summer, and monsoon herb; thrives in warm moist climate
soil: Moist, rich, well-draining loamy soil with high organic matter, pH 6.0-7.0
water: High water requirement; keep soil evenly moist; sensitive to severe drought
seed_rate_and_sowing: Stolon and runner cuttings planted at 30x15 cm spacing
benefits: Soothes indigestion and nausea
Natural oral freshness and cooling carminative
High concentration of antioxidant rosmarinic acid
risks_or_cautions: May aggravate gastroesophageal reflux (GERD) in sensitive individuals
medicinal_uses: Essential oil menthol used in pain-relief balms, inhalers, and digestive churan

diseases.name: Mint Rust (Puccinia menthae)
diseases.symptoms: Dusty orange to chocolate-brown pustules on underside of leaves with corresponding yellow spots on top, leaf distortion and drop.
diseases.cause: Macrocyclic autoecious rust fungus spreading by wind spores during damp humid weather.
organic_treatment: Cut back infected shoots to ground level and burn
Submerge roots in hot water (44°C) for 10 min before transplanting
Neem extract spray
chemical_treatment_type: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation
Replant beds every 2-3 years to fresh fertile soil

name: Betel Leaf
how_to_identify_leaf: Deep green, glossy, heart-shaped (cordate) leaves with obliquely asymmetrical base, prominent curving palmate veins, and distinct pungent spicy aromatic flavor.
how_to_identify_seed_or_fruit: Dioecious woody perennial climber; adventitious clinging roots at nodes; catkin inflorescences rarely setting seeds in commercial paan barejas.
season: Year-round cultivated inside conservatories (bareja / panthota) under 60-70% shade and high humidity
soil: Friable, fertile sandy loam to clayey loam with excellent drainage, rich in humus, pH 7.0-7.5
water: Frequent light daily misting or ditch irrigation; cannot tolerate water stagnation
seed_rate_and_sowing: Stem cuttings of 3-5 nodes with roots planted at 15-20 cm intervals along bamboo trellises
benefits: Traditional post-meal digestive and mouth freshener
Potent antimicrobial and antifungal properties
Rich source of bioactive phenols
risks_or_cautions: Consuming with tobacco or slaked lime causes oral submucous fibrosis and cancer risk; consume plain
medicinal_uses: Warmed leaves applied over chest with castor oil to relieve bronchial congestion in children

diseases.name: Foot Rot & Leaf Rot (Phytophthora parasitica var. piperina)
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked oily dark brown circular lesions on lower leaves expanding rapidly with wet rot; collar rot at vine base causing sudden wilting.
diseases.cause: Soil and water-borne oomycete spreading aggressively during rainy seasons with high soil moisture.
organic_treatment: Drench soil around vine with Trichoderma viride @ 5g/vine mixed with neem cake
Remove and burn wilted vines
chemical_treatment_type: Drench and spray with Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Bordeaux mixture 1%
prevention: Ensure high raised planting ridges for rapid surface drainage
Use disease-free apical vine cuttings
